To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Salmonella enteritidis, the Salmonella Thyphimurim, E. coli and Shigella sonni S are the agents most frequently involved in the etiopathogenesis of the acute gastroenteritises in the case of the Romanian children from the age of 0-14 years and the antibiotic resistance rates are important for the ampicilin, tetracyclines, amoxicilin – clavulane, trimetoprim – sulfametoxazol

in 2012 on the territory of the Iaşi county, Romania and the surroundings the bacterial agents most frequently involved in the etiopathogenesis of the acute gastroenterities in children (0-15 years) were the Salmonella spp., followed by E. Coli, Shigella and Yersinia spp.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the surveillance of the bacterial pathogens that cause AGE in children and the antibiotic resistance of these agents.
a high rate of bacterial pathogens involved (especially Salmonella spp.) in the etiology and the antibiotic resistance rates of these agents.

the surveillance of the agents involved in the etiopathogenesis of the acute gastroenteritides, with the determination of the antibiotic resistance rates and with the establishment of the antibiotic treatment recommendations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in the surveillance period of the acute gastroenteritises, the antibiotic therapy is not recommended for the treatment of the AGE in the case of the Salmonella spp., Yersinia enteroclitica, Campylobacter jejuni, Shigella spp., and E. coli O157: H7.
the antibiotic resistance is high in our region, and the antibiotic therapy should be used in a rational manner.
the antibiotic resistance is a serious public health problem, especially in the case of Salmonella spp. and E. coli, the two most frequent etiologic agents of the acute gastroenteritides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Salmonella spp., the most frequently identified agent, is also the most frequently resistant to ampicillin, trimethopram/ sulfamethoxazole and tetracycline.
we have to be careful when choosing the antibiotics therapy for the acute gastroenteritits in children.
the Salmonella spp., E. coli and Shigella spp. have a significant role in the etiologies of AGE, the antibiotic resistance being high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surveillance programs are essential for the control of the infectious diseases and for a better understanding of their epidemiological profile.
the antibiotic resistance rates of the agents involved in the etiopathogenesis of acute gastroenteritits are high and that they should be taken into account when choosing the antibiotic therapy.
the antibiotic therapy in the case of AGE should be done in a rational manner, according to the local resistance profiles.
